units.title: Drawing: Line, Shape, Value and Space
units.big_idea: Artists use line, value and perspective to create the illusion of form and depth on a flat surface.

units.title: Rhythm, Meter and Beginning Recorder
units.big_idea: Music is organized in time through beat, meter and rhythm, which we can read and write.

units.title: Color and Painting: Landscapes of America
units.big_idea: Color choices create mood, and landscape painters shaped how Americans saw their land.

units.title: Songs of America
units.big_idea: Folk, spiritual and patriotic songs carry the history and ideals of the people who sang them.

units.title: Art of Early America: Craft, Pattern and Print
units.big_idea: Art can preserve culture, tell stories and persuade people.

units.title: Melody, Harmony and Form
units.big_idea: Melodies move by steps and leaps, and harmony and form give music its structure.

units.title: Sculpture and Three-Dimensional Form
units.big_idea: Sculptors shape space and form, and good craftsmanship makes ideas last.

units.title: Instruments of the Orchestra and Composing
units.big_idea: Composers choose instruments, timbre and form to express ideas, and anyone can compose.

units.title: Portfolio, Exhibition and Concert
units.big_idea: Artists and musicians reflect on growth and share their best work with an audience.

objectives: Use different line types expressively
Draw a blind and modified contour drawing

days.title: Line sampler
days.work: Fill a sketchbook page with 12 line types (zigzag, hatched, wavy, broken) and label the mood each suggests.

days.title: Blind contour
days.work: Draw your own hand three times with blind contour, never looking at the paper.

days.title: Modified contour
days.work: Draw a shoe or houseplant with modified contour, glancing at the paper only occasionally.

days.title: Gesture drawing
days.work: Do ten 30-second gesture drawings of a family member in action poses.

days.title: Review & check
days.work: Choose your best contour drawing and write two sentences using art vocabulary about its line quality.

weeks.assessment: Sketchbook check of contour and gesture drawings with written reflection.

objectives: Create a value scale
Shade geometric forms to show light

days.title: Value scale
days.work: Create a 7-step value scale using pencil pressure and another using hatching and cross-hatching.

days.title: Shading forms
days.work: Shade a sphere, cube and cylinder showing highlight, core shadow and cast shadow.

days.title: Observing light
days.work: Light an egg with a flashlight and draw it from observation, matching values.

days.title: Artist study
days.work: Look at a Leonardo da Vinci drawing on Google Arts & Culture and identify how he used value.

days.title: Review & check
days.work: Complete a shaded still life of 2 objects and self-assess using a value checklist.

weeks.assessment: Value scales and shaded still life.

objectives: Use overlapping, size and placement to show depth
Draw in one-point perspective

days.title: Showing depth
days.work: Draw a landscape that uses overlapping, size change and placement to show foreground, middle ground and background.

days.title: One-point perspective
days.work: Draw 3D boxes in one-point perspective with a horizon line and vanishing point.

days.title: Perspective road
days.work: Draw a road or hallway disappearing to a vanishing point with trees or doors along it.

days.title: Place of significance
days.work: Begin a perspective drawing of your street, room or a favorite place.

days.title: Review & check
days.work: Finish the place drawing and label its horizon line and vanishing point.

weeks.assessment: One-point perspective drawing of a personally significant place.

weeks.topic: Drawing project: a detailed observational drawing
objectives: Combine line, value and space in a finished drawing
Explain revisions using art vocabulary

days.title: Choosing a view
days.work: Use a cardstock viewfinder to choose a composition of a corner of your home and make 3 thumbnail sketches.

days.title: Drawing
days.work: Lightly block in the composition with contour lines and perspective.

days.title: Shading
days.work: Add value and texture to the drawing, establishing a focal point.

days.title: Critique and revise
days.work: Get feedback using 'I notice, I wonder' and make one revision.

days.title: Review & check
days.work: Write an artist statement describing your choices and revision, and file the drawing in your portfolio.

weeks.assessment: Drawing project rubric and artist statement.

objectives: Identify steady beat and meter in 2, 3 and 4
Read whole, half, quarter and eighth notes and rests

days.title: Feel the beat
days.work: Pat the steady beat to 3 recordings (a march, a waltz, a pop song) and decide whether each feels in 2, 3 or 4.

days.title: Note values
days.work: Complete the musictheory.net lessons on note durations and clap 8 rhythm cards with counting (1-and-2-and).

days.title: Time signatures
days.work: Draw bar lines into 6 rhythm lines in 2/4, 3/4 and 4/4.

days.title: Rhythm dictation
days.work: Listen to 6 clapped rhythms and write them in notation.

days.title: Review & check
days.work: Read and clap a 4-measure rhythm at sight and take a note-value quiz.

weeks.topic: Syncopation, dotted rhythms and body percussion
objectives: Perform dotted and syncopated rhythms
Improvise a rhythm pattern

days.title: Dotted rhythms
days.work: Learn dotted half and dotted quarter notes and clap patterns from 'America the Beautiful.'

days.title: Syncopation
days.work: Clap and say syncopated patterns (ta ti-ta ti) and find syncopation in a song like 'Ragtime' by Scott Joplin.

days.title: Body percussion ostinato
days.work: Create a 4-beat body percussion ostinato (stomp, pat, clap, snap) and perform it with a recording.

days.title: Bucket drumming
days.work: Improvise 4-measure rhythm solos on a bucket or pot in a call-and-response with a family member.

days.title: Review & check
days.work: Perform the ostinato and an improvised solo and evaluate using a steady-beat rubric.

objectives: Hold and play the recorder with good tone
Read B, A and G on the treble staff
materials: soprano recorder (inexpensive) or free virtual recorder/keyboard app

days.title: Recorder basics
days.work: Learn posture, left-hand position and gentle 'too' tonguing; play B with steady tone.

days.title: A and G
days.work: Learn A and G and play 4-note patterns from a fingering chart.

days.title: Reading the staff
days.work: Identify B, A and G on the staff with flashcards and play 'Hot Cross Buns' and 'Gently Sleep.'

days.title: Practice and record
days.work: Practice 10 minutes and record a performance of 'Hot Cross Buns' to listen back.

days.title: Review & check
days.work: Self-evaluate the recording for tone and rhythm, then play a B-A-G song for an audience.

weeks.topic: Recorder: C, D and E; ensemble playing
objectives: Play C', D' and low E
Perform with others keeping a steady beat

days.title: High C and D
days.work: Learn high C and D and play 'Merrily We Roll Along' and 'Old MacDonald' sections.

days.title: Low E
days.work: Learn low E and play a 5-note warm-up scale with a metronome.

days.title: Ensemble
days.work: Play 'Ode to Joy' (simplified) with a sibling, parent or recording, staying together.

days.title: Practice log
days.work: Practice the unit songs and write a practice log noting a tricky measure and how you fixed it.

days.title: Unit 2 assessment
days.work: Perform two recorder songs and a rhythm reading for family, then evaluate with a performance rubric.

weeks.assessment: Unit 2 recorder and rhythm performance rubric.

objectives: Mix primary, secondary and tertiary colors
Create tints, shades and color schemes
materials: tempera or watercolor paints (red, yellow, blue, white, black)

days.title: Color wheel
days.work: Paint a 12-part color wheel mixing secondary and tertiary colors from primaries.

days.title: Tints and shades
days.work: Paint a tint and shade strip for one color, adding white and black in steps.

days.title: Color schemes
days.work: Paint the same simple design three times with complementary, analogous and monochromatic schemes.

days.title: Brush care
days.work: Practice proper brush cleaning and palette care, then compare how each color scheme changes mood.

days.title: Review & check
days.work: Take a color-theory quiz and write which scheme you prefer and why.

weeks.assessment: Color wheel, scheme studies and quiz.

weeks.topic: The Hudson River School and American landscapes
objectives: Analyze mood and meaning in landscape paintings
Compare criteria across styles
materials: images of Thomas Cole's 'The Oxbow' and Albert Bierstadt's Yosemite paintings (Google Arts & Culture)

days.title: Looking closely
days.work: Study Thomas Cole's 'The Oxbow' for 5 minutes and list what you see, think and wonder.

days.title: Atmospheric perspective
days.work: Identify how Cole and Bierstadt make distant mountains lighter and bluer, then practice with a 3-layer paint study.

days.title: California connection
days.work: Compare Bierstadt's Yosemite painting with a photograph of Yosemite and discuss how the artist exaggerated for effect.

days.title: Comparing styles
days.work: Compare a Hudson River School painting to a Native American landscape design or a modern landscape and discuss how each would be judged.

days.title: Review & check
days.work: Write a paragraph interpreting the mood of one landscape using evidence from color, light and composition.

weeks.assessment: Written interpretation paragraph and atmospheric perspective study.

objectives: Plan and paint a landscape with atmospheric perspective
Use brushes and materials with care

days.title: Watercolor techniques
days.work: Practice wash, wet-on-wet, dry brush and salt texture on a technique sampler.

days.title: Planning
days.work: Sketch a landscape from a photo or outdoors with foreground, middle ground and background.

days.title: Background washes
days.work: Paint the sky and distant layers with light, cool washes.

days.title: Foreground detail
days.work: Paint the middle ground and foreground with warmer, darker colors and detail.

days.title: Review & check
days.work: Evaluate progress with a checklist and note one area to refine.

weeks.assessment: Technique sampler and painting progress check.

objectives: Refine artwork using feedback
Explain choices in an artist statement

days.title: Refining
days.work: Add final details and adjust values to strengthen depth in the landscape.

days.title: Family critique
days.work: Lead a family critique describing, analyzing, interpreting and judging your painting.

days.title: Revision
days.work: Make one revision based on critique feedback.

days.title: Matting
days.work: Mount the painting on a black paper mat with clean edges.

days.title: Review & check
days.work: Write an artist statement and add the painting to your portfolio.

weeks.assessment: Landscape painting rubric and artist statement.

weeks.topic: Native American and early colonial music
objectives: Describe the functions of music in Native American cultures
Compare instruments and song forms

days.title: Native American music
days.work: Listen to a Smithsonian Folkways recording of a Native American song and describe the instruments, vocables and steady drum.

days.title: Purposes of music
days.work: Discuss and chart purposes of songs (ceremony, storytelling, celebration, work) with examples.

days.title: Colonial psalms
days.work: Listen to a 'lining out' psalm from colonial New England and try call-and-response singing.

days.title: Making an instrument
days.work: Make a simple drum or rattle from household items and play a steady-beat pattern.

days.title: Review & check
days.work: Write how music connected to daily life in one culture, citing a recording.

weeks.topic: Songs of the Revolution and the nation
objectives: Sing patriotic songs with accurate pitch
Explain the history and ideals behind each song
materials: lyrics for 'Yankee Doodle,' 'The Star-Spangled Banner,' 'America the Beautiful,' 'My Country, 'Tis of Thee'

days.title: Yankee Doodle
days.work: Learn the history of 'Yankee Doodle' as a British insult turned Patriot anthem and play it on recorder.

days.title: Star-Spangled Banner
days.work: Read about Francis Scott Key and Fort McHenry and sing the first verse with attention to the wide range.

days.title: America the Beautiful
days.work: Learn 'America the Beautiful' and list the geographic images Katharine Lee Bates used.

days.title: Expressive singing
days.work: Choose dynamics and tempo to express the meaning of one song and record a performance.

days.title: Review & check
days.work: Perform two songs and explain the ideal each expresses.

objectives: Explain the history and hidden meanings of spirituals
Perform with expressive qualities
materials: recordings of 'Follow the Drinking Gourd,' 'Swing Low, Sweet Chariot,' 'Wade in the Water'

days.title: Spirituals
days.work: Listen to 'Swing Low, Sweet Chariot' and learn about the origins of spirituals among enslaved African Americans.

days.title: Code songs
days.work: Read the lyrics of 'Follow the Drinking Gourd' and 'Wade in the Water' and discuss their possible hidden meanings.

days.title: Work songs
days.work: Learn a call-and-response work song and explain how rhythm helped people work together.

days.title: Expressive performance
days.work: Compare two performances of the same spiritual and note differences in tempo, dynamics and timbre.

days.title: Review & check
days.work: Sing a spiritual with chosen expressive qualities and write about the performers' intent.

weeks.topic: Folk songs of a growing nation
objectives: Learn folk songs about westward travel
Perform a family sing-along with accompaniment
materials: lyrics for 'Oh! Susanna,' 'Erie Canal,' 'Shenandoah,' 'Sweet Betsy from Pike'

days.title: Erie Canal
days.work: Learn 'Low Bridge, Everybody Down (Erie Canal)' and identify verse and chorus.

days.title: Shenandoah
days.work: Sing 'Shenandoah' and discuss how the melody's long phrases create a feeling of longing.

days.title: Oh! Susanna
days.work: Learn Stephen Foster's 'Oh! Susanna' and play its melody on recorder or virtual keyboard.

days.title: Accompaniment
days.work: Add a simple body-percussion or drum accompaniment to one folk song.

days.title: Unit 4 assessment
days.work: Lead a family sing-along of 3 American songs and write a reflection on what the songs teach about history.

weeks.topic: Native American art: pattern and symbolism
objectives: Analyze symbols and patterns in Native American art
Create a design inspired by traditional pattern principles
materials: images of Navajo weaving, Pueblo pottery and Haudenosaunee beadwork (Smithsonian NMAI)

days.title: Looking at art
days.work: Examine images of Pueblo pottery, Navajo weavings and Haudenosaunee beadwork and describe their patterns.

days.title: Symbols and meaning
days.work: Read museum labels explaining what certain designs mean and why some symbols are sacred and should not be copied.

days.title: Pattern design
days.work: Design your own symmetrical geometric pattern on graph paper using personal symbols.

days.title: Paper weaving
days.work: Weave a paper mat in two colors to understand over-under structure.

days.title: Review & check
days.work: Write how art preserves culture and explain the meaning of your own symbols.

objectives: Interpret messages in portraits
Compare folk art and academic art

days.title: Reading a portrait
days.work: Analyze Copley's 'Paul Revere' portrait and list clues about his job and status.

days.title: Folk art
days.work: Compare a professional portrait with a folk-art portrait by Ammi Phillips and discuss different criteria for judging them.

days.title: Facial proportions
days.work: Learn basic facial proportions and draw a guided self-portrait from a mirror.

days.title: Symbolic objects
days.work: Add objects to your self-portrait that show your interests, as colonial portraitists did.

days.title: Review & check
days.work: Compare your interpretation of the Copley portrait with a family member's and write about the differences.

weeks.assessment: Self-portrait with symbolic objects and interpretation comparison.

objectives: Analyze how prints spread ideas
Make a relief print
materials: foam trays or craft foam sheets

days.title: Prints that persuade
days.work: Study Paul Revere's Boston Massacre engraving and Franklin's 'Join, or Die' and explain how prints spread messages.

days.title: Designing a print
days.work: Design a simple image with a message about a cause you care about, remembering the print will be reversed.

days.title: Carving
days.work: Press the design into a foam plate with a dull pencil, checking line depth.

days.title: Printing an edition
days.work: Roll ink and pull an edition of 4 prints, numbering and signing them.

days.title: Review & check
days.work: Choose your best print and explain its message and the care taken with tools.

objectives: Analyze quilts as art and history
Combine ideas into an original quilt square design
materials: images of historic quilts (Gee's Bend, Harriet Powers's Bible Quilt)

days.title: Quilts as stories
days.work: Study Harriet Powers's Bible Quilt and a Gee's Bend quilt and discuss how quilts tell stories.

days.title: Block patterns
days.work: Draw 3 traditional quilt block patterns (Log Cabin, Flying Geese, Star) on graph paper.

days.title: Original square
days.work: Combine ideas to design an original paper quilt square that tells something about your family.

days.title: Family quilt
days.work: Join squares from family members into a paper 'quilt' showing unity and variety.

days.title: Unit 5 assessment
days.work: Present the quilt square and answer questions about how early American art carried messages.

objectives: Identify melodic contour and intervals
Read notes on the treble staff

days.title: Melodic contour
days.work: Listen to 4 melodies and draw their contour shapes with lines.

days.title: Steps, skips and leaps
days.work: Identify steps, skips and leaps in 'Ode to Joy' and 'Twinkle, Twinkle' notation.

days.title: Note naming
days.work: Practice naming notes on the treble staff with musictheory.net exercises until scoring 90%.

days.title: Recorder: F-sharp and low D
days.work: Learn low D and F-sharp on recorder and play a D-major warm-up.

days.title: Review & check
days.work: Take a note-naming and interval quiz and play an 8-measure melody.

objectives: Hear the difference between major and minor
Play a major scale
materials: Chrome Music Lab Piano Roll or Chords

days.title: Major vs. minor
days.work: Listen to 6 excerpts and identify major or minor, describing the mood of each.

days.title: Scale patterns
days.work: Build a C major scale using whole and half steps on a virtual keyboard.

days.title: Playing scales
days.work: Play the G major scale on recorder (G-A-B-C-D-E-F#-G) slowly and evenly.

days.title: Minor melody
days.work: Play 'Hot Cross Buns' in major, then change it to minor on a keyboard and compare.

days.title: Review & check
days.work: Take a listening quiz on major and minor and perform the G major scale.

weeks.topic: Harmony: rounds, partner songs and chords
objectives: Sing in harmony in a round
Identify I and V chords

days.title: Rounds
days.work: Sing 'Row, Row, Row Your Boat' and 'Frère Jacques' as rounds with family members.

days.title: Partner songs
days.work: Sing two partner songs together ('This Old Man' and 'Skip to My Lou') to create harmony.

days.title: Chords
days.work: Use Chrome Music Lab Chords to build I and V chords in C and listen for when they change in a song.

days.title: Two-chord song
days.work: Accompany a familiar two-chord song (e.g., 'Clementine') by playing I and V on a virtual keyboard or ukulele.

days.title: Review & check
days.work: Write the chord changes (I or V) above lyrics of a song and perform it.

weeks.topic: Musical form: AB, ABA, rondo and theme and variations
objectives: Identify musical forms by listening
Map the form of a piece
materials: recordings: Mozart 'Twinkle Variations,' Beethoven 'Für Elise,' Mouret 'Rondeau'

days.title: AB and ABA
days.work: Listen to two short pieces and label sections A and B using colored shapes.

days.title: Rondo
days.work: Listen to Mouret's 'Rondeau' and map the ABACA form with a listening map.

days.title: Theme and variations
days.work: Listen to Mozart's 'Twelve Variations on Ah vous dirai-je, Maman' and describe how 3 variations change the theme.

days.title: Movement map
days.work: Create a movement routine that changes with each section of 'Für Elise' to show its form.

days.title: Unit 6 assessment
days.work: Take a listening assessment identifying form, major/minor and melodic contour.

objectives: Transform 2D materials into 3D forms
Use positive and negative space

days.title: Paper techniques
days.work: Practice curling, folding, scoring, fringing and tab joints to make a paper techniques sampler.

days.title: Sculptor study
days.work: Look at Alexander Calder and Ruth Asawa sculptures and discuss positive and negative space.

days.title: Abstract sculpture
days.work: Build a freestanding abstract paper sculpture at least 8 inches tall.

days.title: Viewing from all sides
days.work: Photograph the sculpture from 4 angles and adjust any weak side.

days.title: Review & check
days.work: Write about how your sculpture uses positive and negative space.

weeks.topic: Clay or salt dough sculpture: planning and building
objectives: Use pinch, coil and slab methods
Plan a functional or expressive form
materials: air-dry clay or homemade salt dough

days.title: Pinch pot
days.work: Make a pinch pot and practice even wall thickness.

days.title: Coils and slabs
days.work: Make a coil and a slab test piece and join pieces using score and slip.

days.title: Planning
days.work: Sketch a sculpture (animal vessel or expressive figure) combining ideas from two inspirations.

days.title: Building
days.work: Build the sculpture's main form using the chosen methods.

days.title: Review & check
days.work: Add texture and details and cover with plastic; note what to finish next week.

weeks.assessment: Technique test pieces and sculpture plan.

objectives: Finish a sculpture with quality craftsmanship
Argue for safe and effective presentation

days.title: Smoothing
days.work: Smooth rough edges of the dry sculpture carefully with fine sandpaper or a damp sponge.

days.title: Painting
days.work: Paint the sculpture with a planned color scheme.

days.title: Sealing
days.work: Seal the sculpture and clean all tools and work space.

days.title: Display plan
days.work: Write how the sculpture should be displayed safely (pedestal, label, lighting) and why.

days.title: Review & check
days.work: Present the sculpture to family and explain revisions made during the process.

weeks.assessment: Sculpture craftsmanship rubric and display plan.

objectives: Create sculpture from found or natural materials
Interpret how artists use materials to communicate

days.title: Artist study
days.work: Look at Andy Goldsworthy's nature art and Louise Nevelson's assemblages and discuss materials and meaning.

days.title: Collecting
days.work: Collect natural or recycled materials and sort them by color, shape and texture.

days.title: Environmental sculpture
days.work: Build an ephemeral outdoor sculpture from natural materials and photograph it.

days.title: Assemblage
days.work: Assemble a small found-object sculpture in a shoebox lid painted one color.

days.title: Unit 7 assessment
days.work: Write a comparison of your two sculptures and present photos in your portfolio.

objectives: Identify orchestra families by sight and sound
Describe timbre
materials: Britten's 'Young Person's Guide to the Orchestra' recording

days.title: Orchestra families
days.work: Learn the four instrument families and sort 16 instrument pictures by family.

days.title: Young Person's Guide
days.work: Listen to Britten's 'Young Person's Guide to the Orchestra' and list instruments as they are featured.

days.title: Timbre
days.work: Play the Classics for Kids instrument game and describe timbres with adjectives (bright, mellow, brassy).

days.title: Making an instrument
days.work: Build a homemade instrument (rubber-band guitar, straw oboe or bottle xylophone) and explain how it makes sound.

days.title: Review & check
days.work: Take a listening quiz identifying 8 instruments by sound.

weeks.topic: Program music: telling stories with sound
objectives: Explain how composers use expressive qualities to tell stories

courses.subject: PE
courses.title: PE 5
courses.description: Fifth-grade physical education that refines throwing, catching, dribbling, striking and rhythmic movement skills through lead-up games for soccer, flying disc, basketball, volleyball and softball, plus jump rope and folk dance. Fifth grade is a California Physical Fitness Test (FITNESSGRAM) year, so the course opens with a baseline fitness check, teaches the components of health-related fitness and heart-rate monitoring, and closes with a personal fitness plan and post-test. Every week includes a warm-up and cool-down, skill practice with critical cues, a game or challenge, and a sportsmanship focus; most activities need only a backyard, park or driveway.
courses.framework: California Physical Education Model Content Standards (2005); 2009 California Physical Education Framework

courses.subject: HEALTH
courses.title: Health 5
courses.description: Grade 5 health education aligned to the 2008 California Health Education Content Standards, which focus fifth grade on Growth and Development, Nutrition and Physical Activity, and Alcohol, Tobacco and Other Drugs, with supporting Personal and Community Health (hygiene, sleep, dental care). Students study body systems, nutrition labels and fitness, healthy body image and media literacy, then a seven-week puberty unit covering hormones, the reproductive systems, menstruation and emotional changes (parents preview materials and may opt out, consistent with CA Education Code). The year closes with tobacco, vaping, alcohol, cannabis and medicine safety, refusal skills, and a health-advocacy campaign.
courses.framework: 2008 California Health Education Content Standards (Grade 5: Growth and Development; Nutrition and Physical Activity; Alcohol, Tobacco and Other Drugs; plus Personal and Community Health); 2019 CA Health Education Framework

standards.H-5.8.1.N: Advocate for healthy eating and physical activity at home and in the community.

standards.H-5.1.3.G: Explain the role of hormones and the endocrine system in puberty.
standards.H-5.1.4.G: Identify the structures and functions of the male and female reproductive systems.
standards.H-5.1.5.G: Explain menstruation, nocturnal emissions and other normal pubertal changes.
standards.H-5.1.6.G: Recognize that the timing of puberty varies and that each person grows at their own rate.
standards.H-5.1.7.G: Explain why personal hygiene becomes more important during puberty.

standards.H-5.3.1.G: Identify trusted adults and valid sources of information about puberty and growth.

units.title: Health Skills and Body Systems
units.big_idea: Healthy choices are skills we practice, and our body systems work together as we grow.

units.title: Nutrition for Growing Bodies
units.big_idea: A growing body needs balanced nutrients and fewer added sugars, sodium and saturated fats.

units.title: Physical Activity and Fitness
units.big_idea: Daily activity builds every component of fitness and supports healthy growth.

units.title: Body Image and Media
units.big_idea: Healthy bodies come in many shapes and sizes; media images are often not real.

units.title: Personal Health and Hygiene
units.big_idea: Daily hygiene, sleep and check-ups keep a changing body healthy.

units.title: Puberty: Growth and Development
units.big_idea: Puberty is a normal stage of growth that happens to everyone at their own pace.

units.title: Tobacco, Nicotine and Vaping
units.big_idea: Nicotine is addictive, and tobacco and vaping products harm the lungs, heart and brain.

units.title: Alcohol, Cannabis, Inhalants and Medicines
units.big_idea: Alcohol and other drugs affect the developing brain; medicines are safe only when used correctly.

units.title: Influences, Refusal and Decisions
units.big_idea: Recognizing pressure and practicing refusal skills helps us stay drug-free.

units.title: Advocacy and Year Review
units.big_idea: We can use what we know to help family and friends make healthy choices.

weeks.topic: Health skills and the wellness triangle

Name the eight health skills

days.title: Review & check

days.title: Strength tests

days.work: Create a 7-day plan with at least 60 minutes daily including muscle- and bone-strengthening activity 3 days.

days.title: Review & check

days.title: Review & check

objectives: Describe healthy body image

days.title: Dieting dangers
days.work: Read a KidsHealth article on dieting and list why skipping meals or fad diets harm growing kids.

days.title: Kind words
days.work: Practice replacing body-shaming comments with respectful statements in 5 scenario cards.

days.title: Review & check
days.work: Write a paragraph on healthy body image and answer a 5-question check.

Analyze ads targeting kids

days.work: Learn 6 advertising techniques (bandwagon, celebrity, fun, health claims, giveaways, beautiful people) and find examples in magazines.

days.title: Edited images
days.work: Watch a short before-and-after photo-retouching video and discuss how it affects body image.

days.title: Food ads
days.work: Analyze two kids' food commercials: target audience, techniques and what they leave out.

days.title: Gender messages
days.work: Compare toy or clothing ads aimed at boys vs. girls and note stereotypes about how bodies should look.

days.title: Review & check
days.work: Create a counter-ad that promotes healthy body image or a healthy food honestly.

days.title: Sweat and oil
days.work: Learn how sweat and oil glands become more active in puberty and why body odor and acne happen.

days.title: Skin care
days.work: Read about gentle face washing and acne myths; write a simple morning and evening skin routine.

days.title: Deodorant vs. antiperspirant

days.title: Hair and nails

days.title: Review & check

Build a daily routine

days.title: Review & check

days.title: Review & check
days.work: Answer questions from the question box with a parent and complete a 5-question check.

objectives: Explain how the pituitary gland starts puberty

days.title: Review & check

objectives: Communicate about puberty with a parent or trusted adult

days.work: Write three conversation starters for talking with a parent about puberty.

days.title: Body autonomy

days.title: Review & check

objectives: Summarize physical, emotional and social changes
Show respect for differences in development

days.title: Concept map
days.work: Build a concept map linking hormones, physical changes, emotions, hygiene and trusted adults.

days.title: Stop teasing
days.work: Role-play responding to teasing about early or late development.

days.title: Self-care kit
days.work: Assemble or list a personal self-care kit for school or travel.

days.title: Advice column
days.work: Write answers to three advice-column questions from fictional 5th graders about puberty.

days.title: Review & check
days.work: Take the Growth and Development unit test and discuss results with a parent.

objectives: Describe effects of tobacco on the body

days.work: Read about nicotine, tar and carbon monoxide and label a body diagram with their effects.

days.title: Addiction and the brain
days.work: Learn how nicotine changes the brain's reward system and why teens get addicted faster.

days.title: Secondhand smoke
days.work: Research secondhand smoke effects and CA smoke-free laws.

days.title: Review & check
days.work: Complete a tobacco-effects quiz.

objectives: Describe the risks of vaping
Identify vaping myths

days.work: Sort 10 vaping statements (e.g., 'it's just water vapor') into myths and facts with evidence.

days.title: Flavors and packaging
days.work: Analyze images of vape packaging and explain how flavors and colors target young people.

days.title: Real norms
days.work: Read survey data showing most youth do not vape and make a bar graph.

days.title: Review & check
days.work: Write a short public service announcement correcting one vaping myth.

objectives: Analyze tobacco marketing
Demonstrate refusal skills

days.title: Historic ads
days.work: Compare historical cigarette ads with today's vape marketing and identify persuasion techniques.

days.title: Refusal steps
days.work: Learn refusal strategies: say no clearly, give a reason, suggest an alternative, walk away.

days.title: Role-play
days.work: Role-play 4 scenarios refusing a vape from an older kid or friend.

days.title: Assertive vs. passive
days.work: Practice assertive body language and tone compared with passive and aggressive responses.

days.title: Review & check
days.work: Perform a refusal role-play for a parent and take the tobacco unit test.

objectives: Describe effects of alcohol on the brain and body
Explain impaired judgment

days.title: Alcohol pathway
days.work: Trace alcohol's path through the body on a diagram and note effects on the brain, liver and stomach.

days.title: Coordination demo
days.work: Try simple tasks (walking a line, tossing a ball) while spinning first to model impaired coordination, then discuss.

days.title: Developing brain
days.work: Read about why alcohol is especially harmful to the developing brain and why the legal age is 21.

days.title: Short vs. long term
days.work: Make a chart of short- and long-term effects of alcohol.

days.title: Review & check
days.work: Complete an alcohol facts quiz.

objectives: Describe the effects of cannabis on young people
Identify dangers of inhalants

days.title: Cannabis facts
days.work: Read a NIDA for kids article on marijuana and list effects on memory, learning and reaction time.

days.title: Edibles danger
days.work: Learn why cannabis edibles can look like candy and what to do if you find one.

days.title: Inhalants
days.work: Read warning labels on household products and explain why sniffing them can cause sudden death.

days.title: Laws and norms
days.work: Learn that cannabis is illegal under 21 in CA and review data showing most youth don't use it.

days.title: Review & check
days.work: Complete a matching quiz on cannabis and inhalant effects.

objectives: Distinguish prescription and OTC medicines
Explain medicine misuse

days.title: Rx vs. OTC
days.work: Compare a prescription label and an OTC Drug Facts label and identify each part.

days.title: Dosage math
days.work: Use a Drug Facts chart to find the correct dose by age and weight in 3 practice problems.

days.title: Misuse
days.work: Discuss why sharing prescriptions or taking extra doses is dangerous.

days.title: Safe storage
days.work: Inspect your home's medicine storage with a parent and learn the Poison Control number (1-800-222-1222).

days.title: Review & check
days.work: Complete a medicine-safety scenario quiz.

objectives: Identify trusted adults and resources
Explain how to help someone affected by substance use

days.title: Who can help?
days.work: List trusted adults and community resources (doctor, school counselor, Poison Control, faith leader) for drug concerns.

days.title: Family affected
days.work: Read a story about a family member's alcohol problem and discuss feelings and where kids can get support.

days.title: Help script
days.work: Write a script for telling a trusted adult you found a vape or pills.

days.title: Resource card
days.work: Design a wallet-size resource card with key numbers.

days.title: Review & check
days.work: Take the Alcohol and Other Drugs unit test.

objectives: Analyze influences on substance-use decisions
Identify protective factors

days.title: Influence web
days.work: Make a web of influences (family, friends, media, culture, community) on decisions about drugs.

days.title: Peer pressure types
days.work: Identify spoken, unspoken and online peer pressure in 6 scenarios.

days.title: Alcohol ads
days.work: Analyze an alcohol advertisement for target audience and hidden messages.

days.title: Protective factors
days.work: List protective factors in your life (family rules, activities, goals) and how they help.

days.title: Review & check
days.work: Write a paragraph analyzing the strongest influence on you and how to respond.

objectives: Apply the decision process to ATOD scenarios
Evaluate consequences

days.title: Values
days.work: Rank personal values and explain how they guide decisions about drugs.

days.title: Decision chart 1
days.work: Use the decision chart for a sleepover scenario where someone brings alcohol.

days.title: Decision chart 2
days.work: Use the decision chart for a scenario involving a friend's prescription pills.

days.title: Negotiation
days.work: Practice negotiating a safe alternative activity with a friend.

days.title: Review & check
days.work: Complete a decision-making assessment with a new scenario.

objectives: Set a drug-free goal
Demonstrate multiple refusal strategies

days.title: Drug-free goal
days.work: Write a personal drug-free goal with reasons and supports.

days.title: Refusal toolbox
days.work: Practice 6 refusal strategies (broken record, humor, change subject, leave, give facts, suggest alternative).

days.title: Record a skit
days.work: Write and record a 1-minute refusal skit.

days.title: Coping without drugs
days.work: List healthy ways to deal with stress, boredom and sadness.

days.title: Review & check
days.work: Perform a refusal skill demonstration scored with a rubric.

objectives: Choose a health message
Plan an advocacy project

days.title: Choose a topic
days.work: Pick a topic (drug-free, vaping myths, healthy drinks, daily activity) and state a clear health-enhancing message.

days.title: Research
days.work: Gather 3 facts from valid sources to support the message.

days.title: Audience
days.work: Identify the audience (younger siblings, family, community group) and plan how to reach them.

days.title: Draft materials
days.work: Draft a poster, brochure or short video script.

days.title: Review & check
days.work: Peer- or parent-review the draft with an advocacy checklist.

objectives: Produce campaign materials
Practice presenting

days.title: Final product
days.work: Create the final poster, brochure or video.

days.title: Call to action
days.work: Add a clear call to action and a source list.

days.title: Rehearse
days.work: Rehearse a 3-minute presentation of the campaign.

days.title: Goal check
days.work: Review your nutrition, activity and drug-free goals from the year and record progress.

days.title: Review & check
days.work: Present a dress rehearsal to a parent and revise based on feedback.

objectives: Present the campaign
Reflect on growth and health goals

days.title: Present
days.work: Present the campaign to family, a co-op or community group.

days.title: Year review game
days.work: Play a review game covering nutrition, fitness, hygiene, puberty and ATOD.

days.title: Final assessment
days.work: Take the end-of-year health assessment.

days.title: Summer plan
days.work: Write a summer health plan with activity, sleep and hygiene goals.

days.title: Reflect
days.work: Write a reflection on how you have grown this year and what health skill helps you most.
